title: Psalm 33 — YHWH looks down from the heavens on all the sons of the human

verdicts.reasoning: rannĕnû ṣaddîqîm baYHWH layšārîm nāʾwâ tĕhillâ; no superscription in MT (LXX 'of David'), so MT = ASV numbering. Exact.
hôdû laYHWH bĕkinnôr bĕnēbel ʿāśôr zammĕrû-lô: ASV instruments. Exact.
šîrû-lô šîr ḥādāš hêṭîbû naggēn bitrûʿâ. Exact.
kî-yāšār dĕbar-YHWH wĕkol-maʿăśēhû beʾĕmûnâ. Exact.

citations: Sakenfeld, The Meaning of Hesed in the Hebrew Bible (1978)
verdicts.reasoning: ʾōhēb ṣĕdāqâ ûmišpāṭ ḥesed YHWH mālʾâ hāʾāreṣ: solitary ḥesed 'kindness' (central chesed-solitary, founder point E), with the loyalty sense and ASV/NRSV given in commentary; 'earth' for the universal scope. Changed line verified.

citations: BDB s.v. rûaḥ 1 (breath of the mouth)
verdicts.reasoning: bidbar YHWH šāmayim naʿăśû ûbĕrûaḥ pîw kol-ṣĕbāʾām: 'skies' for the created sky; rûaḥ 'breath' parallel to dābār (ASV 'breath'); ṣĕbāʾām 'their host' = the stars. Exact.
kōnēs kannēd mê hayyām nōtēn bĕʾôṣārôt tĕhômôt: MT kannēd 'as a heap' (ASV/KJV; Ex 15:8) kept, LXX hōs askon / NRSV 'as in a bottle' recorded. Correct MT-baseline application.
yîrʾû mēYHWH kol-hāʾāreṣ mimmennû yāgûrû kol-yōšĕbê tēbēl: ʾereṣ || tēbēl, 'earth'. Exact.
kî hûʾ ʾāmar wayyehî hûʾ-ṣiwwâ wayyaʿămōd. Exact.
YHWH hēpîr ʿăṣat-gôyim hēnîʾ maḥšĕbôt ʿammîm. Exact.
ʿăṣat YHWH lĕʿôlām taʿămōd maḥšĕbôt libbô lĕdōr wādōr. Exact.
ʾašrê haggôy ʾăšer-YHWH ʾĕlōhāyw: suffixed ʾĕlōhîm 'whose Elohim', no article (overlay rule); ʾašrê 'Blessed' with NJPS 'Happy' recorded. Exact.

miššāmayim hibbîṭ YHWH rāʾâ ʾet-kol-bĕnê hāʾādām: 'heavens' (dwelling, glossed by mĕkôn-šibtô in v 14) under the founder's register ruling; 'all the sons of the human' as genesis-woh Gen 11:5 (checked) under central ha-adam (founder point B). The reception note keeps the canon's 'flying craft' reading out of the line; 'from the heavens' is the ASV wording.
mimmĕkôn-šibtô hišgîaḥ ʾel kol-yōšĕbê hāʾāreṣ: mākôn 'fixed place' (1 Kgs 8:39), hišgîaḥ 'gaze'. Exact.
hayyōṣēr yaḥad libbām hammēbîn ʾel-kol-maʿăśêhem: ASV construal of yaḥad, alternative recorded; verbal yōṣēr not forced into the epithet entry. Exact.
ʾên-hammelek nôšāʿ bĕrob-ḥāyil gibbôr lōʾ-yinnāṣēl bĕrob-kōaḥ. Exact.
šeqer hassûs litšûʿâ: 'a false hope for victory' (NRSV sense; literal 'a lie for deliverance' and ASV given). Defensible.
hinnēh ʿên YHWH ʾel-yĕrēʾāyw lamyaḥălîm lĕḥasdô: 'kindness' as v 5. Changed line verified.

citations: Wolff, Anthropology of the Old Testament (1974), ch. 2
verdicts.reasoning: lĕhaṣṣîl mimmāwet napšām ûlĕḥayyôtām bārāʿāb: nepeš 'life' where a life is saved from death, confirmed by the parallel 'keep them alive'; follows the Kings/Ezekiel overlays. Changed line verified.
napšēnû ḥikkĕtâ laYHWH: 'Our soul waits' (self as subject; ASV kept). Exact.
kî-bô yiśmaḥ libbēnû kî bĕšēm qodšô bāṭāḥnû. Exact.
yĕhî-ḥasdĕkā YHWH ʿālênû kaʾăšer yiḥalnû lāk: 'kindness' as v 5. Changed line verified.

glossaryReview.reasoning: Every site verified: YHWH; 'Yah' (Ps 147:1, 20); the article follows the Hebrew (anarthrous Ps 8:6; Eccl 3:10, 13; articular Eccl 3:11, 14, 15, 17, 18); 'El', 'Eloah' and 'Shaddai' as in stable job-woh (38:41; 40:2, 9); 'our Lord' for ʾădōnênû. Direct is right: these are presentation rules over explicit Hebrew forms. Flagged only for founder point A (Ps 8:6 'Elohim' against the canon's 'the Elohim'). Reviewer view: keep the anarthrous form. The Hebrew has no article, the rule matches job-woh 1:9 and the Kings clause 2, and departing from the canon's wording here is evidence that the line is not canon-driven.

Site-by-site application of the founder's Kings-wave register ruling, checked verse by verse: physical sky 'skies' (Ps 8:2, 4, 9; 19:2, 7; 33:6; 147:8; Prov 8:27; Eccl 3:1; Job 37:3); dwelling or cosmic height 'heavens' (Ps 33:13 || mĕkôn-šibtô; 139:8 against She'ol). Ps 8:2 ('splendor upon the skies') is the closest call and is argued from v 4. Direct is appropriate.

'earth' at universal and cosmic sites (kol-hāʾāreṣ; ʾereṣ || tēbēl) is the reading of ASV, NRSV and NJPS, and the isaiah-woh precedent. 'land' is kept for territory (Prov 10:30; Job 37:13) and the stable 'wings of the land' (Job 37:3 = 38:13). Every site was checked. Agree with founder point C: promote the clause to central eretz in a later diff.

The lexical mapping is accurate and consistent with central ha-adam / ben-adam (direct) and with GEN-WOH-11:5 'the sons of the human' (checked). ʾĕnôš 'a mortal' and ʾîšîm 'O men' are sound. Flagged for founder point B. The articular/anarthrous split ('the sons of the human' / 'the sons of human', Prov 8:4, 31) is formally exact but yields stiff English, and in Biblical Hebrew the two forms are not distinct in sense. The corpus is now split three ways ('sons of men' ASV / canon-EN; 'children of men' 1 Kgs 8:39; 'sons of the human' Gen 11:5). Reviewer view: accept the editor's forms for coherence with the central entries, and align 1 Kgs 8:39 to them. If the founder prefers idiom, revert all bĕnê (hā)ʾādām sites together to 'the sons of men' with a string swap, and leave the singular ben-adam untouched.

citations: Wolff, Anthropology of the Old Testament (1974), ch. 2
glossaryReview.reasoning: The 'life' / 'soul' split was checked at all six sites. 'life' where a life is delivered from death or forfeited (Ps 33:19 || 'keep them alive'; Prov 8:36 in the life/death antithesis), as in the Kings and Ezekiel overlays. ASV 'soul' is kept for the self (Ps 19:8; 33:20; 139:14; Prov 10:3), with the appetite sense in commentary. Direct is defensible: BDB lists both senses.

Inferred is the honest class: the traditional English of Eccl 3:21 is 'spirit'. The lexical evidence is real. BDB and HALOT give rûaḥ 'breath (of life)'; NJPS has 'lifebreath' at Eccl 3:21; and vv 19-21 argue about the one rûaḥ that humans and beasts share (Gen 6:17; 7:15, 22). Lower-case 'spirit' at Ps 139:7 follows NRSV and NJPS. 'wind' (Job 37:21; Ps 147:18) and 'breath of his mouth' (Ps 33:6) are uncontroversial.

Applied correctly at every listed site. MT Psalm numbering was verified (superscription = v 1 in Pss 8, 19; run into v 1 in Ps 139). The one vowel-only exception at Ps 8:2 is declared and justified: the MT impv. tĕnâ has no syntax after ʾăšer. Eccl 3:21 keeps the Masoretic articular participles and fully records the interrogative reading of LXX, Vulgate, ASV, NRSV and NJPS. Non-blocking: add 'KJV' to the Eccl 3:21 clause as the English witness to the MT pointing ('the spirit of man that goeth upward'), so that the entry does not suggest that every English version departs from the MT.
appliesTo +12 matches appliesToAdded exactly (verified against base); every site carries the ref and follows the register rule.

+10 sites verified, including articular bĕnê hāʾādām on the GEN-WOH-11:5 precedent. If founder point B reverts the plurals, drop PSA-WOH-33:13 and ECC-WOH-3:10, 18, 19, 21 from this op and keep the singular sites.
+12 sites verified. The article follows the Hebrew; the rule is recorded in the overlay, parallel to Kings clause 2.
+4 sites verified (Ps 33:7; Prov 8:24, 27, 28). Non-blocking: the plural is 'the deeps' at Ps 33:7 and 'depths' at Prov 8:24; both are ASV, but a single English plural would be tidier.

citations: Sakenfeld, The Meaning of Hesed in the Hebrew Bible (1978)
glossaryReview.reasoning: The extension is correct and the changed lines were verified (Ps 33:5, 18, 22; 147:11; Job 37:13). 'kindness' is lexically defensible for solitary ḥesed (Glueck; Sakenfeld). Flagged for founder point E only, because the Psalter has about 120 further occurrences. Reviewer view: confirm 'kindness' now, before the Psalms grow, so that the rendering does not drift. It is the central wohChoice, it is consistent with genesis-woh and Kings, and the loyalty sense is carried in commentary. 'steadfast love' (NRSV) is the main alternative.
+Ps 33:6 'all their host' (the stars, astral sense already in the wohChoice); the suffix form is correctly not expanded to 'host of the heavens'. Verified.

reviewerReport.lensLeakageCheck: All 22 lines checked. 33:13-14 render šāmayim / mĕkôn-šibtô with no vantage-point language; the 'flying craft' reading is confined to the note. No flags.
reviewerReport.escalationReportAdjustments: Initial verdicts on all 205 verses, the 17 overlay entries and the 16 central-diff ops were formed from the chapters, the Leningrad source files, the overlays, the diff, the 2.83.0 base and the canon-quotation file before wave-w1-editor-report.md was opened. After reading it, no verdict changed. The report's list of the three canon-coincident lines (section 1) confirmed the two commentary revisions: at Job 37:18 and Prov 8:30 the notes cite only the canon's French, whose wording matches the line, and omit the canon's English ('the sky'; 'as one brought up with him'), which does not. Prov 8:22 already shows the correct treatment. The report's six-pair Ketiv/Qere count was independently confirmed.

founderDecisionRecommendations.A-Ps-8:6-article-on-Elohim: Keep 'a little less than Elohim' without the article. The Hebrew mēʾĕlōhîm is anarthrous, the rule matches job-woh 1:9 and Kings clause 2, and the reception note already gives the canon's 'the Elohim'. Differing from the canon here is useful evidence that the line follows the Hebrew.
founderDecisionRecommendations.B-bene-(ha)adam: Accept 'the sons of the human' / 'the sons of human' for coherence with central ha-adam / ben-adam and GEN-WOH-11:5, and align 1 Kgs 8:39 ('the children of men') to it. The cost is stiff English at Prov 8:4, 31, and the Hebrew article on bĕnê (hā)ʾādām carries no difference in sense. If the founder prefers idiom, revert every plural site together to 'the sons of men' (string swap; drop the plural refIds from the ha-adam and ben-adam ops). Do not mix the two.
founderDecisionRecommendations.C-eretz-cosmic-earth: Agree. Promote the 'earth' scope clause (isaiah-woh + Writings) to central eretz in a dedicated later diff, after the parallel appliesTo merges have landed.
founderDecisionRecommendations.D-proper-names: Accept English forms in the four Writings books. Job 37 must match the stable job-woh chapters, and the four books must agree. Record the corpus practice as genre-split (narrative transliterated, poetry and prophets English) or settle it in one corpus-wide decision. Do not leave it implicit.
founderDecisionRecommendations.E-chesed-kindness: Confirm 'kindness' for solitary ḥesed now, before the Psalter grows (about 120 occurrences). It is the central wohChoice, consistent with genesis-woh and Kings, and lexically sound (Glueck; Sakenfeld). The loyalty sense stays in commentary, and the fixed pair ḥesed wĕʾĕmet stays under chesed-v-emet.
founderDecisionRecommendations.F-Job-37:18-clouds: No decision needed: 'clouds' rests on BDB/HALOT, KJV and stable job-woh 38:37, and 'strong' (not 'solid') keeps the line neutral. The reviewer asks for one transparency sentence (JOB-WOH-37:18 revise; shechaqim op revise): the canon's English edition reads 'the sky', so the canon is itself divided.

paragraphs.text: רַנְּנ֣וּ צַ֭דִּיקִים בַּֽיהוָ֑ה לַ֝יְשָׁרִ֗ים נָאוָ֥ה תְהִלָּֽה׃

i18n.en: Shout for joy in YHWH, you righteous; praise is fitting for the upright.

notes.official: *rannĕnû* 'Shout for joy'; *nāʾwâ tĕhillâ* 'praise is fitting'. The psalm has no superscription in the MT (the LXX adds 'Of David'), so the MT and ASV verse numbers coincide.

paragraphs.text: הוֹד֣וּ לַיהוָ֣ה בְּכִנּ֑וֹר בְּנֵ֥בֶל עָ֝שׂ֗וֹר זַמְּרוּ־לֽוֹ׃

i18n.en: Give thanks to YHWH with the harp; sing praises to him with the ten-stringed psaltery.

notes.official: *kinnôr* 'harp' (ASV; a lyre); *nēbel ʿāśôr* 'the ten-stringed psaltery' (ASV 'the psaltery of ten strings').

paragraphs.text: שִֽׁירוּ־ל֭וֹ שִׁ֣יר חָדָ֑שׁ הֵיטִ֥יבוּ נַ֝גֵּ֗ן בִּתְרוּעָֽה׃

i18n.en: Sing to him a new song; play skillfully, with a shout of joy.

paragraphs.text: כִּֽי־יָשָׁ֥ר דְּבַר־יְהוָ֑ה וְכָל־מַ֝עֲשֵׂ֗הוּ בֶּאֱמוּנָֽה׃

i18n.en: For the word of YHWH is upright, and all his work is done in faithfulness.

paragraphs.text: אֹ֭הֵב צְדָקָ֣ה וּמִשְׁפָּ֑ט חֶ֥סֶד יְ֝הוָ֗ה מָלְאָ֥ה הָאָֽרֶץ׃

i18n.en: He loves righteousness and justice; the earth is full of the kindness of YHWH.

notes.official: *ʾōhēb ṣĕdāqâ ûmišpāṭ* 'He loves righteousness and justice' (central `tzedakah-u-mishpat-justice-pair`). *ḥesed YHWH mālʾâ hāʾāreṣ* 'the earth is full of the kindness of YHWH'. *ḥesed* is 'kindness' under the central `chesed-solitary-covenant-kindness` entry, as in genesis-woh and 1-2 Kings (ASV 'lovingkindness'; NRSV 'steadfast love'). The word combines loyalty within a relationship with active goodness (Glueck, *Hesed in the Bible*, 1967; Sakenfeld, *The Meaning of Hesed in the Hebrew Bible*, 1978). The same rendering at vv 18 and 22. *hāʾāreṣ* is the whole earth (`eretz-earth-and-land-scope-writings`).

paragraphs.text: בִּדְבַ֣ר יְ֭הוָה שָׁמַ֣יִם נַעֲשׂ֑וּ וּבְר֥וּחַ פִּ֝֗יו כָּל־צְבָאָֽם׃

i18n.en: By the word of YHWH the skies were made, and all their host by the breath of his mouth.

notes.official: *bidbar YHWH šāmayim naʿăśû* 'By the word of YHWH the skies were made': the created sky of Gen 1, 'skies' (central `shamayim`; ASV 'heavens'). *ûbĕrûaḥ pîw kol-ṣĕbāʾām* 'and all their host by the breath of his mouth'. *rûaḥ* is parallel to *dābār* 'word', the breath that carries speech, so 'breath' (ASV; `ruach-wind-breath-spirit-writings`). *ṣĕbāʾām* 'their host' are the stars (cf. Gen 2:1; Isa 40:26), the astral sense of the central `tzeva-ha-shamayim-host-of-the-heavens-divine-council-cross-corpus` entry.

paragraphs.text: כֹּנֵ֣ס כַּ֭נֵּד מֵ֣י הַיָּ֑ם נֹתֵ֖ן בְּאֹצָר֣וֹת תְּהוֹמֽוֹת׃

i18n.en: He gathers the waters of the sea together as a heap; he lays up the deeps in storehouses.

notes.official: *kōnēs kannēd mê hayyām* 'He gathers the waters of the sea together as a heap'. MT *kannēd* 'as a heap' recalls the sea and river crossings (*nēd*, Ex 15:8; Josh 3:13, 16). The LXX (*hōs askon*), the Targum and the Vulgate read *kannōd* 'as in a wineskin', which NRSV adopts ('as in a bottle'); the ASV and KJV follow the MT, and so does the line (`mt-baseline-versification-and-psalm-numbering-writings`). *tĕhômôt* 'the deeps' (central `tehom`), laid up *bĕʾôṣārôt* 'in storehouses'.

paragraphs.text: יִֽירְא֣וּ מֵ֭יְהוָה כָּל־הָאָ֑רֶץ מִמֶּ֥נּוּ יָ֝ג֗וּרוּ כָּל־יֹשְׁבֵ֥י תֵבֵֽל׃

i18n.en: Let all the earth fear YHWH; let all the inhabitants of the world stand in awe of him.

notes.official: *kol-hāʾāreṣ* || *kol-yōšĕbê tēbēl* 'all the earth ... all the inhabitants of the world': universal scope, so 'earth' (`eretz-earth-and-land-scope-writings`).

paragraphs.text: כִּ֤י ה֣וּא אָמַ֣ר וַיֶּ֑הִי הֽוּא־צִ֝וָּ֗ה וַֽיַּעֲמֹֽד׃

i18n.en: For he spoke, and it came to be; he commanded, and it stood.

notes.official: *kî hûʾ ʾāmar wayyehî* 'For he spoke, and it came to be': *wayyehî* recalls the creation formula of Gen 1:3.

paragraphs.text: יְֽהוָ֗ה הֵפִ֥יר עֲצַת־גּוֹיִ֑ם הֵ֝נִ֗יא מַחְשְׁב֥וֹת עַמִּֽים׃

i18n.en: YHWH brings the counsel of the nations to nothing; he frustrates the plans of the peoples.

paragraphs.text: עֲצַ֣ת יְ֭הוָה לְעוֹלָ֣ם תַּעֲמֹ֑ד מַחְשְׁב֥וֹת לִ֝בּ֗וֹ לְדֹ֣ר וָדֹֽר׃

i18n.en: The counsel of YHWH stands forever, the plans of his heart to all generations.

paragraphs.text: אַשְׁרֵ֣י הַ֭גּוֹי אֲשֶׁר־יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהָ֑יו הָעָ֓ם ׀ בָּחַ֖ר לְנַחֲלָ֣ה לֽוֹ׃

i18n.en: Blessed is the nation whose Elohim is YHWH, the people whom he has chosen as an inheritance for himself.

notes.official: *ʾašrê* 'Blessed' (ASV) is an exclamation, 'O the happiness of' (NJPS 'Happy'), distinct from *bārûk* 'blessed (by YHWH)'. The ASV word is kept, with the difference recorded here; the same at Prov 8:32, 34. *ʾăšer-YHWH ʾĕlōhāyw* 'whose Elohim is YHWH': the suffixed form is left untranslated, without an article (`elohim-as-translation`; `divine-names-convention-writings`). *bāḥar lĕnaḥălâ lô* 'he has chosen as an inheritance for himself'.

paragraphs.text: מִ֭שָּׁמַיִם הִבִּ֣יט יְהוָ֑ה רָ֝אָ֗ה אֶֽת־כָּל־בְּנֵ֥י הָאָדָֽם׃

i18n.en: From the heavens YHWH looks down; he sees all the sons of the human.

notes.official:
*miššāmayim hibbîṭ YHWH* 'From the heavens YHWH looks down'. Here *šāmayim* is the place of YHWH's dwelling, glossed in v 14 as *mĕkôn-šibtô* 'the place of his dwelling', so the line has 'heavens' under the register clause of the central `shamayim` entry, as at 1 Kgs 8:30, 39 (`shamayim-register-application-writings`). *kol-bĕnê hāʾādām* 'all the sons of the human': the articular phrase is rendered as genesis-woh renders it at Gen 11:5, under the central `ha-adam` entry (ASV 'all the sons of men'; 1 Kgs 8:39 woh 'the children of men'; `adam-enosh-ish-human-terms-writings`).

**Wheel of Heaven reading (reception note, not a translation claim).** The Book Which Tells the Truth (ch. 3) quotes vv 13-14 ('Yahweh looketh from heaven; he beholdeth all the sons of men. From the place of his habitation he looketh upon all the inhabitants of the earth') and reads them as the creators watching the doings of humanity from their flying craft, as they always have. The lines render *šāmayim* and *mĕkôn-šibtô* as the Hebrew names them and make no claim about the vantage point.

paragraphs.text: מִֽמְּכוֹן־שִׁבְתּ֥וֹ הִשְׁגִּ֑יחַ אֶ֖ל כָּל־יֹשְׁבֵ֣י הָאָֽרֶץ׃

i18n.en: From the place of his dwelling he gazes upon all the inhabitants of the earth —

notes.official: *mimmĕkôn-šibtô hišgîaḥ* 'From the place of his dwelling he gazes'. *mākôn* 'fixed place, site' is used of YHWH's dwelling in the heavens (1 Kgs 8:39, 43, 49) and of the sanctuary (Ex 15:17; 1 Kgs 8:13). *hišgîaḥ* 'gaze, look intently' is rare (Isa 14:16; Song 2:9). *kol-yōšĕbê hāʾāreṣ* 'all the inhabitants of the earth' is universal (`eretz-earth-and-land-scope-writings`). See the reception note at v 13.

paragraphs.text: הַיֹּצֵ֣ר יַ֣חַד לִבָּ֑ם הַ֝מֵּבִ֗ין אֶל־כָּל־מַעֲשֵׂיהֶֽם׃

i18n.en: he who fashions the hearts of them all, who considers all their works.

notes.official: *hayyōṣēr yaḥad libbām* 'he who fashions the hearts of them all' (ASV). *yaḥad* 'together, alike' may go with the verb ('who fashions their hearts alike') or with the suffix ('of them all'); the line keeps the ASV. *yōṣēr* is the potter's verb of Gen 2:7. It is rendered as a verb here because it takes an object; the central `yotzer-bereshit-creator-of-beginnings-cross-corpus-hebrew-bible-hekhalot-divine-epithet`, which cites the verse, governs the absolute epithet only. *hammēbîn* 'who considers'.

paragraphs.text: אֵֽין־הַ֭מֶּלֶךְ נוֹשָׁ֣ע בְּרָב־חָ֑יִל גִּ֝בּ֗וֹר לֹֽא־יִנָּצֵ֥ל בְּרָב־כֹּֽחַ׃

i18n.en: No king is saved by the greatness of an army; a mighty man is not delivered by great strength.

paragraphs.text: שֶׁ֣קֶר הַ֭סּוּס לִתְשׁוּעָ֑ה וּבְרֹ֥ב חֵ֝יל֗וֹ לֹ֣א יְמַלֵּֽט׃

i18n.en: A horse is a false hope for victory, and by its great strength it does not deliver.

notes.official: *šeqer hassûs litšûʿâ* 'A horse is a false hope for victory' (lit. 'a lie for deliverance'; ASV 'a vain thing for safety').

paragraphs.text: הִנֵּ֤ה עֵ֣ין יְ֭הוָה אֶל־יְרֵאָ֑יו לַֽמְיַחֲלִ֥ים לְחַסְדּֽוֹ׃

i18n.en: Behold, the eye of YHWH is on those who fear him, on those who hope for his kindness,

notes.official: *hinnēh ʿên YHWH* 'Behold, the eye of YHWH'; *lamyaḥălîm lĕḥasdô* 'on those who hope for his kindness' (central `chesed-solitary-covenant-kindness`, as v 5).

paragraphs.text: לְהַצִּ֣יל מִמָּ֣וֶת נַפְשָׁ֑ם וּ֝לְחַיּוֹתָ֗ם בָּרָעָֽב׃

i18n.en: to deliver their life from death, and to keep them alive in famine.

notes.official: *lĕhaṣṣîl mimmāwet napšām* 'to deliver their life from death'. Where *nepeš* is the life that is saved from death, the corpus renders 'life', following the Kings and Ezekiel overlays (`nefesh-scope-writings`; ASV and NRSV 'their soul'). The parallel *ûlĕḥayyôtām bārāʿāb* 'and to keep them alive in famine' confirms the sense.

paragraphs.text: נַ֭פְשֵׁנוּ חִכְּתָ֣ה לַֽיהוָ֑ה עֶזְרֵ֖נוּ וּמָגִנֵּ֣נוּ הֽוּא׃

i18n.en: Our soul waits for YHWH; he is our help and our shield.

notes.official: *napšēnû ḥikkĕtâ laYHWH* 'Our soul waits for YHWH': here *nepeš* is the self that waits and hopes, and the ASV 'soul' is kept (`nefesh-scope-writings`). *ʿezrēnû ûmāginnēnû hûʾ* 'he is our help and our shield'.

paragraphs.text: כִּי־ב֭וֹ יִשְׂמַ֣ח לִבֵּ֑נוּ כִּ֤י בְשֵׁ֖ם קָדְשׁ֣וֹ בָטָֽחְנוּ׃

i18n.en: For our heart rejoices in him, because we have trusted in his holy name.

paragraphs.text: יְהִֽי־חַסְדְּךָ֣ יְהוָ֣ה עָלֵ֑ינוּ כַּ֝אֲשֶׁ֗ר יִחַ֥לְנוּ לָֽךְ׃

i18n.en: Let your kindness, YHWH, be upon us, as we have hoped in you.

notes.official: *yĕhî-ḥasdĕkā YHWH ʿālênû* 'Let your kindness, YHWH, be upon us' (central `chesed-solitary-covenant-kindness`; ASV 'lovingkindness').
